title: Emergency Follow-Up Visits in Continuity of Care — Primary Care Provider Assignment
content:
**Training note, Primary Care Provider Assignment: emergency follow-up visits on a continuity-of-care referral.**

**Q. What are emergency follow-up visits?**
Visits added to a continuity-of-care referral for a member who has recently used the emergency room for emergencies. They are added to the window visits once those have been rounded up to a whole visit, before the visits recorded are held between the floor of one visit and the ceiling.

**Q. What is counted?**
The member's paid emergency-room claims for emergencies — claims in the emergency room (emergency) category booked on the member's **Medicaid Managed Care Membership** — with a service date in the recent-use window of **6 months**. Emergency-room claims in the non-emergency category are not counted.

**Q. How many visits are added?**

| Paid emergency-room claims for emergencies in the last 6 months | Emergency follow-up visits added |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 2 (the larger follow-up allowance) |
| Exactly 1 | 1 (the smaller follow-up allowance) |
| None | 0 |

**Q. How is the window read?**
It is a trailing period counted back from the handling date in whole months: a claim is inside it when fewer than 6 whole months separate its service date from the handling date, so a claim dated exactly 6 months back is outside it.

**Q. Worked answers (hypothetical, handling date 15 September 2026)?**

- Paid emergency claims on 4 May and 29 August 2026: two, so 2 visits added.
- Paid emergency claims on 15 March and 29 August 2026: 15 March is exactly 6 months back and outside, leaving one, so 1 visit added.
- One paid emergency-room claim in the non-emergency category on 29 August 2026 and no other: none counted, no visit added.
